title: How Trump Gave the Worst Polluters a Free Pass
partialText: The president temporarily waived clean-air rules for industrial facilities that spew cancer-causing gases. Then his appointees worked to gut the regulations altogether.

title: 5 Takeaways From Our Investigation of Trump’s Waivers for Polluters
partialText: Chemical plants and other industrial facilities had been required to curb their toxic emissions. A New York Times investigation shows how they got out of it.

title: In U.S. Gas Talks With Kremlin, Hidden Financing for Alaska Project Emerges
partialText: Interviews and documents show a Russian energy giant secretly funded a U.S. firm. The deal has been discussed in talks to end the war in Ukraine.

title: Trump Officials Seek Block on Alaska Senate Race Results if the Republican Dan Sullivan Loses
partialText: The department, in a highly unusual lawsuit, argued that confusion over candidates with similar names could taint the election result.

title: Why Legal Experts See the Justice Dept.’s Alaska Election Challenge as Dubious
partialText: No obvious legal authority supports a pre-emptive effort to block the certification of Alaska’s Senate election if the Republican incumbent narrowly loses.

title: How Vivek Ramaswamy’s Ruthless Ad in Ohio Divided Republicans
partialText: The fallout from Vivek Ramaswamy’s brutal spot targeting his Democratic rival in the Ohio governor’s race showed that even in the Trump era, a political attack can be seen as going too far.

title: Why Democrats Could Find It Hard to Win the Senate Despite Their Strong Polls
partialText: Democrats are increasingly optimistic about the midterms. But they are being outspent by Republicans. And they are trying to compete in states that favored President Trump by large margins.

title: Iran in ‘Advanced Stages’ of Planning Attacks Against Americans, Officials Say
partialText: The U.S. government has ordered diplomats and other federal employees to leave Saudi Arabia. It is also drawing down staff at other missions in the region.

title: Looting Left Damage and Fear on Paradise Street in Marseille
partialText: Looters ravaged a storied commercial avenue in France’s second-largest city. Its merchants fear that more unrest could follow.

title: They Were Accused of Illegal Fishing. They Ended Up in ICE Detention.
partialText: In states like Florida, officers who hand out fishing citations and inspect produce have been deputized by Immigration and Customs Enforcement, expanding the reach of President Trump’s deportation campaign.
